title: R’ Yehoshua ben Memal, a Tanna
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites [Nazir 56b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.56b.9-10): R’ Elazar (ben Shamua) said, “When I went to Ardaskiya, I found R’ Yehoshua ben Peter Rosh”—[Tosefta Nazir, chapter 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Nazir.5.3), has R-Y ben Petira—“sitting and discussing halakhah before R’ Meir. He asked me, ‘Are you acquainted with R’ Yehoshua ben Memal?’ I answered, ‘Yes.’ He (R’ Elazar) said to him, ‘Thus R’ Yehoshua bar Memal told me in R’ Yehoshua’s name.’” Hyman says Tosefta Nazir describes him, through R’ Meir, as a master of halakhot. At the end of [Tosefta Ohalot, chapter 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Oholot.4.7), Hyman says it reads, erroneously, that he was a master of crafts.[^3]

notes.text: Hyman explicitly writes Elazar ben Shamua, while the checked Nazir text reads Eliezer. His parenthetical speaker assignment and awkward first-person exchange are retained rather than silently harmonized. The supplied כשעת in the Ohalot clause remains corrupt.

The whole saved Machon Mamre Tosefta Ohalot4 scalar6 has abbreviated R-A and R-M, and full Rabbi Yehudah ben Petirush, not Hyman’s Yehoshua ben Peter Rosh/Petira. It includes the acquaintance question and בעל מלאכות, but does not explain supplied כשעת. The earlier Nazir Eliezer reading versus Hyman’s explicit Elazar ben Shamua remains inherited, not newly inspected. Hyman’s parenthetical R-A speaker assignment and first-person shifts remain, without harmonizing interlocutors. Full Rabbi from the DIFFERENT Ohalot name is not transferred to the heading or abbreviated titles. Master of crafts remains literal, not silently changed to master of halakhah.

Hyman’s printed article (vol. II, p. 646) calls the Ohalot reading erroneous and has “master of halakhot” for his report of Tosefta Nazir. The supplied transcription instead has the unclear כשעת and singular הלכה. The checked Nazir 56b names Rabbi Eliezer and keeps Yehoshua ben Peter Rosh. In its exchange, the narrator asks the question and is answered “Yes.” The consulted Machon Mamre Tosefta Nazir 5 calls the narrator Rabbi Elazar and, in brackets, names Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira and reads בעל הלכות. The consulted Ohalot 4 has Rabbi Yehudah ben Petirush and בעל מלאכות. These readings describe the witnesses separately and leave Hyman’s speaker assignment and names as his account.
